 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE PURNENDU SINGH  ORAL ORDER 13 04-09-2025 Heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner and the learned APP for the State.

2. The present quashing application has been filed on behalf of the petitioner for quashing of order dated 27.10.1999 passed in Complaint Case No.C980/99, Tr.No.697/99 by the learned J.M. Ist Class, Sasaram, whereby cognizance has been taken under Sections 406, 408, 409, 420 and 120(B)
of IPC and the same is pending before the court of the learned SDJM, Sasaram in Complaint Case No.C980/99, Tr. No.1756/15.
3.

As per the allegation made in the complaint petition, the accused persons, who were posted on different posts in M/S Vaibhav Finance & Investment Ltd. (hereinafter to Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.44677 of 2015(13) dt.04-09-2025 be referred as the 'Company') misappropriated total Rs.38,750/- of the complainant (O.P.No.2) along with the interest, which was deposited in the Company.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the petitioner had joined M/S Vaibhav Finance & Investment Ltd. on 10.09.1995 as the Additional Director but he resigned on 01.08.1997 and the same was accepted by the Board of Director and a news/notice was circulated in the daily newspaper "Prabhat Khabar" informing that Mr. Vinay Kishore Prasad (petitioner) has resigned from the post of Additional Director and no longer any consumer is required to contact him or his acts would be binding upon the company.

He submitted that the present complaint petition has been filed on 07.10.1999 nearly two years after his resignation, the petitioner has been implicated leading to malacious prosecution on the frivilous grounds.
Learned counsel further submitted that no specific allegation has been alleged against the petitioner.
No evidence supports that there has been cash transaction with the petitioner rather it is the co-accused Vinay Tiwari against whom such allegations rests.

5. Heard the parties.
6.
The present complaint petition had been filed in the Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.44677 of 2015(13) dt.04-09-2025 court of the learned CJM, Sasaram, which was transferred in the court of the learned J.M. Ist class, Sasaram for inquiry and trial.

The statements of the complainant and other witnesses were recorded and considering their statements, as well as, the materials available on the record, the cognizance was taken on 27.10.1999 under Sections 409 of IPC.
7.
No one appears on behalf of the complainant.
8. The obvious caveat being that the allegations, even if having a civil flavor to them, must prima facie disclose an overwhelming element of criminality.

In the absence of the element of criminality,
if both civil and criminal cases are allowed to continue, it will definitely amount to abuse of the process of the Court, which the Courts have always tried to prevent by putting a stop to any such criminal proceeding, where civil proceedings have already been instituted with regard to the same issue, and the element of criminality is absent.
If such element is absent, the prosecution in question would have to be quashed.

9. The Apex Court in the case of Yogendra Yadav & Ors. Vs. State of Jharkhand & Anr. reported in (2014) 9 SCC 653 in Paragraph Nos. 4 & 5 has held as under:
"4.

entities.text: Yogendra Yadav & Ors. Vs. State of Jharkhand & Anr. reported in (2014) 9 SCC 653
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now, the question before this Court is whether this Court can compound the offences Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.44677 of 2015(13) dt.04-09-2025 under Sections 326 and 307 IPC which are non- compoundable?
Needless to say that offences which are non-compoundable cannot be compounded by the court.
Courts draw the power of compounding offences from Section 320 of the Code.

The said provision has to be strictly followed (Gian Singh v. State of Punjab [Gian Singh v.
State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303 : (2012) 4 SCC (Civ) 1188 : (2013) 1 SCC (Cri) 160 : (2012) 2 SCC (L&S) 988] ).

entities.text:
Gian Singh v. State of Punjab [Gian Singh v.
State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303 : (2012) 4 SCC (Civ) 1188 : (2013) 1 SCC (Cri) 160 : (2012) 2 SCC (L&S) 988
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, in a given case, the High Court can quash a criminal proceeding in exercise of its power under Section 482 of the Code having regard to the fact that the parties have amicably settled their disputes and the victim has no objection, even though the offences are non- Binay Kishore Sinha @ Binoy Kishore ... vs State Of Bihar And Anr on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192870267/
2 compoundable.

entities.text: Binay Kishore Sinha @ Binoy Kishore ... vs State Of Bihar And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In which cases the High Court can exercise its discretion to quash the proceedings will depend on facts and circumstances of each case.
Offences which involve moral turpitude, grave offences like rape, murder, etc. cannot be effaced by quashing the proceedings because that will have harmful effect on the society.
Such offences cannot be said to be restricted to two individuals or two groups.
If such offences are quashed, it may send wrong signal to the society.

However, when the High Court is convinced that the offences are entirely personal in nature and, therefore, do not affect public peace or tranquillity and where it feels that quashing of such proceedings on account of compromise would bring about peace and would secure ends of justice, it should not hesitate to quash them.
In such cases, the prosecution becomes a lame prosecution.
Pursuing such a lame prosecution would be waste of time and energy.

That will also unsettle the compromise and obstruct restoration of peace."
5.

In Gian Singh [Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303 : (2012) 4 SCC (Civ) 1188 :
(2013) 1 SCC (Cri) 160 : (2012) 2 SCC (L&S) 988] this Court has observed that: (SCC p. 340, para 58) "58.

sentences.text: Where the High Court quashes a criminal proceeding having regard to the fact that the dispute between the offender and the victim has Patna High Court CR.

MISC. No.44677 of 2015(13)
dt.04-09-2025 been settled although the offences are not compoundable, it does so as in its opinion,
continuation of criminal proceedings will be an exercise in futility and justice in the case demands that the dispute between the parties is put to an end and peace is restored; securing the ends of justice being the ultimate guiding factor."
Needless to say that the above observations are applicable to this Court also."
10. The record reveals that a compromise has been entered between the parties in the year, 2000 and the petitioner has been granted anticipatory bail.

The record also reveals that an amount amounting to Rs.38,500/- has already been paid to the complainant, pursuant to the compromise between the complainant and the Managing Director of the Company on 07.06.2002.
As such, the order taking cognizance dated 27.10.1999 is not sustainable in the eye of law in respect of the petitioner, having been passed without application of judicial mind.
11. That being the position, the order taking cognizance dated 27.10.1999 is set aside and quashed.

(Purnendu Singh, J) chn/-
